level_description: Real-World Schemas, Round 2 (More production JSON Schemas and documented API/platform constraints -- Docker Compose, AWS RDS, GitHub branch protection, and common observability/alerting convention. Deliberately built to have little-to-no deterministic bypass: almost every field here is a genuine input an LLM would have to supply, validated against another independently-generated field, not a derived output a real system would compute post-hoc.)

RW2_docker_compose_resources.name: Docker Compose Service Resource Limits
RW2_docker_compose_resources.description: Adapted from the Docker Compose Specification's deploy.resources block: a service's resource limits must be >= its reservations (the scheduler reserves at minimum, and caps at maximum) -- the same real relational rule as Kubernetes, in a different, equally common config format.

prompts.system: You are a container orchestration tool generating a validated Docker Compose service resource block. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate CPU and memory reservations/limits for a service. Limits must never be lower than reservations.

memory_limit_mb.description: Memory limit in MB (must be >= reservation)

RW2_rds_storage_autoscaling.name: AWS RDS Storage Autoscaling Configuration
RW2_rds_storage_autoscaling.description: Adapted from AWS RDS's documented storage-autoscaling rule (docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_PIOPS.Autoscaling.html): max_allocated_storage must be >= allocated_storage (equal disables autoscaling, greater enables it). A real, citable AWS API validation rule, not a synthetic invention.

prompts.system: You are the AWS RDS control plane generating a validated storage-autoscaling configuration. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate an RDS instance storage configuration with autoscaling enabled.

RW2_branch_protection_rule.name: GitHub Branch Protection Rule
RW2_branch_protection_rule.description: Adapted from GitHub's branch protection REST API (docs.github.com/en/rest/branches/branch-protection): required_approving_review_count is an integer field GitHub's own UI/API caps at 6. No cross-field arithmetic here, deliberately -- this case isolates the plain range/enum enforcement gap in a CFG baseline, without any deterministic assignment to lean on.

prompts.system: You are a source control platform generating a validated branch protection rule. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate a branch protection rule for a production branch with code review requirements.

enforce_admins.description: Whether the rule also applies to admins

RW2_monitoring_alert_rule.name: Observability Alert Rule Thresholds
RW2_monitoring_alert_rule.description: Modeled on common alerting-platform convention (Prometheus Alertmanager, Datadog monitors): a critical threshold must be at least as severe as the warning threshold for the same metric. Not tied to one vendor's schema file, but a standard, widely-documented practice across the observability industry -- described honestly as such rather than over-cited to one spec.

prompts.system: You are a monitoring platform generating a validated alert rule. Output ONLY raw, valid JSON.
prompts.user: Generate an alert rule for a system metric with warning and critical thresholds.
